name: Ajita Kesakambala
dates_notes: Placed broadly among the early Śramaṇa teachers reported in Buddhist sources. The name is not attached to a surviving independent text or secure biography.
evidence_basis: Buddhist reports of the six contemporary teachers and parallel recensional evidence.
core_thesis: Ajita Keśakambala is reported as denying post-mortem survival and karmic recompense, treating the person as dissolved at death rather than as a continuing soul or stream subject to retribution. This makes him a significant early materialist or annihilationist interlocutor, distinct from later Cārvāka traditions whose positions are also largely reconstructed from opponents. The report is not an authorial statement, and it does not license a detailed reconstruction of Ajita's cosmology, epistemology, or social teaching.
